institutionName: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Due to covid the exchange options in Europe was quite limited. Another thing was that a lot of the universities in USA you had to be on the bachelor, and I was on my first year of the master. 
The third things was language requirements, I also looked at Paris, Munich and South America, but all had requirements for getting a certain grade on the language test.
It also needed to be a university with no GPA or lower than 7 grade GPA requirement, as my GPA at the application time was 6,8... So all Japanese and Korean universities and American and Australian universities were not available for me. 
Lastly, I spent a lot of time looking into the courses available, and I was looking for places where I could get courses about nanomaterials etc.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think HKUST was quite good at sending out information about everything before hand, so it was easy arriving. They even did most of the work handling student visa.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Before hand HKUST had fixed everything according to student visa and medical insurance (it was part of the rent money). So at arrival and orientation days it was just following the signs and then you got your student-ID as well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You could get a shared dorm room at one of their many dorms. They actually also had a dorm outside the campus area.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
So, if you wanted to cook your self you had to buy pans, pots, plates, cutlery etc. because the kitchen only consisted of a microwave, a hob, fridge and water fountain. 
But there were different canteens where the food actually was fairly cheap (about 30-40 DKK for a full meal with a drink). The restaurants was a bit more expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
They have many different sport facilities that was easy to book and free to use (KU could learn from this!).
The university is very on a very beautiful location, out by the water - I could hear it from my window in the evening. Everything is very grand and big and build up a mountain, so there are a lot of escalators and elevators you have to go up to get from the dorms to the classrooms. 
The dorms are a bit old and worn down. You share the room with one other exchange student. It is not like living at a kollegie in DK, there are not as much social things at the dorms.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
We arrived, checked in at our dorm rooms, we just had to show a document. 
At orientation day they showed us around and told us about all the important information. Later that same day we could collect our student-ID.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They answered their emails quite fast, and you could always go to their office and talk with them.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got into all the classes I applied for. They had a swapping period the first two weeks, and the courses I wanted to swap is was able to.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just read the emails they send and do as most as you can before leaving, then everything is going to go quite smoothly at arriving. I can really recommend staying at a hotel a few days before arriving to sleep out the jetlag.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Generally, the level is lower than I DK. The 5th year course I took, which is the highest level you could take, could very well have been a 3rd year course in DK. 
The hard part was mostly getting a lot of assignments, projects and presentations at the same time.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It was very different. The lectures was a teacher talking and going through slides for 80 min without a break. Some courses it was even 3 hours without a break... The practice classes was just a master or PhD student going through solution of the assignments for 50 min and not us actually having time to get help how to solve thing, also practice classes was ONLY 50 min a week. 
There was not really any feedback on the assignments, you just got a grade, which in my opinion is not very development oriented, but just "I have to do this and get It done" from the teachers side.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
CENG5840: Nanomaterials for Chemical Engineering Applications
CHEM4420: Statistical Machine Learning for Chemical Data Analysis 
LIFS4320: Data Science for Biology and Medicine
LIFS3240: Introduction to Neurobiology 
PHYS3042: Structure and Properties of Crystalline Solids

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend the Nanomaterials for Chemical Engineering Applications course and Statistical Machine Learning for Chemical Data Analysis course. The lectures were sweet and listening, but also the most interesting of the courses I had.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to get a new backpack and jacket due to mold because of the humid dorm rooms.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
The food at the canteens and fast food restaurants were cheaper than I expected. Also public transportation was really really cheap.
The cinema was also quite cheap, and I could even get student discount (so about 50 DKK for a ticket)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were planned trips for the exchange students in the first month only. But we were out seeing a temple, visiting Lamma island and painting ceramics. They sometimes had opening to join sport clubs, but the places was so limited that it was impossible to get a place.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend looking into the free sport facilities. I brought my own tennis racket and balls (you could also borrow) and play twice a week. Their indoor and outdoor swimming pools was also great. Outside of the university I will recommend hiking trips and kayaking in the Sai Kung area.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go hiking and kayaking, a lot of HK is nature. 
Go visit Victoria harbor and Victoria peak, the Big Buddha, Ozone bar, Ladies market, Kowloon walled city park, go to the cinema.
Take the ferry between HK island and the TST area, also take the ferries to Lamma island and Cheung Chau. 
You get free entrance to the science museum and other some other things with your student-ID. 

If you want to stay at a hotel in the city I will recommend finding a hotel in the Central area or Mongkok area, not TST.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was fairly easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: You really have to be the one engaging and talking. They are quite shy and don't engage much.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The thing with not being able as much to influence the teaching (80 min without a break is mean, only getting grades and not any feedback etc.), not being able to talk with the teacher and just "accept" that the students doesn't have anything to say was frustrating.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food was incredible! Also how helpfull the global office was at the university.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Save up enough money so you can enjoy the time fully. HK is a bit more expensive than DK, and there are also great opportunities for traveling to the nearby countries. 
2. If you go in the spring semester the weather are going to change from 13 degrees to 30-something degrees and quite humid during those 4 months. So bring some dehumidifier balls for your clothes and things. 
3. Go out and experience the city when it is most alive, in the evening. The classes aren't that hard, so use your time to have fun as well

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Generally they are a bit more "controlling" in drinking/partying on campus and especially in the dorms (where it is forbidden). And also the dorm life is not like living a kollegium, it feels a bit more like a hostel.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Getting a break from the same routine of KU. I was away on my 8th semester, so it was nice to have a change in the way of having courses and exams. 
And also just experiencing a new place, learning in different environments, and being able to travel around afterwards.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: How the whole teaching system/hierarchy is build up.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
